summary: Cache-side memory pressure and load stalls limit the matmul, rather than external DRAM bandwidth.
reasoning: Memory SOL is 70.14% versus compute throughput of 38.53%. L2 throughput reaches 74.96%, while DRAM throughput is only 15.24%, indicating a cache-dominated memory bottleneck. Long-scoreboard stalls account for 62.21% of active-warp cycles.

root_causes.cause: Global loads use memory sectors inefficiently, increasing traffic through the cache hierarchy.

evidence.interpretation: Global loads use only half of each sector on average.
Warps frequently wait for dependencies on global-memory loads.

fixes.fix: Specialize operand load layouts for the actual input strides so adjacent lanes access contiguous, aligned elements.
fixes.rationale: Improved coalescing can reduce sector traffic and the service time of operand loads.

root_causes.cause: Small 32×64 output tiles limit intra-program operand reuse, placing repeated operand-load demand on L2.

evidence.interpretation: L2 is the most heavily utilized reported memory level.
Most requests hit L2, consistent with repeated cached operand accesses.
External DRAM bandwidth is not saturated.

fixes.fix: Benchmark larger output tiles, such as 64×64 or 64×128, while tuning num_warps and checking occupancy.
fixes.rationale: Larger tiles reuse each loaded operand across more output elements, reducing cache traffic per FLOP; occupancy checks guard against excessive resource usage.
